correctness.rationale: The Gao--Shan increment can be written as a fixed base key minus two selected-index counts. Under either one-sided uniqueness condition, every selection causes one uniform group decrement and at most one point decrement, so two-level heaps reproduce the exact greedy minima in O(log |D|) time per choice. The final-layer prefix/suffix decomposition is a bijection in both overlap and nonoverlap cases, giving direct output-sensitive enumeration. The finite artifact checks both mechanisms against naïve exhaustive computations.

originality.rationale: Qualified to the best of our knowledge. Gao--Shan arXiv:2609.18237 states a direct implementation cost O(N2^2 + N3 lambda3) based on repeated packet scans and exhaustive longest-word scanning. Targeted literature searches did not locate the grouped priority implementation, the direct shadow-product enumerator, or the resulting O(N2 log N2 + mu3 lambda3) bound. Standard data-structure ideas are excluded from the novelty claim. The recent source and uninspected full text of the older binary Congero--Zeger paper leave residual originality risk.

value.rationale: The result removes the quadratic middle-layer rescan and replaces exhaustive enumeration of all N3 longest words by work proportional to the requested mu3 outputs, turning the stated deterministic construction into a near-linear/output-sensitive implementation in its main search spaces.
